intent: Test linux_configuration/scripts/single_use/fixes/lib/bt_report.sh to 100% line coverage and take it off the shell-coverage allowlist, continuing the fixes/lib coverage campaign.
scope: Non-goal: refactoring pacman_hook_stall_harness.sh, whose six libs are already gated at 100% with no exemption
Non-goal: the remaining 15 untested fixes/lib libs, handled in later commits
changes: Added lib_test_core.sh: PASS/FAIL tally, _t_eq/_t_contains/_t_lacks assertions, a mktemp -d sandbox wiped on EXIT, a FAKE_BIN stub dir on PATH, and _t_stub/_t_unstub. _t_unstub runs `hash -r`, because removing a stub file alone does not drop bash's cached executable path.

Added bt_harness.sh: sources lib_test_core.sh, sources the real scripts/lib/common.sh for the production log_*/has_cmd helpers (verified inert at source time), and redefines _btctl and apply_fix verbatim from fix_bluetooth.sh since those live in the entry script rather than in any lib.

Added _t_only_path, which drops PATH to FAKE_BIN alone: every tool these libs call (usbreset, pactl, lsusb, ...) genuinely exists on this host, so a prepended stub dir cannot exercise a 'not installed' branch.

Added test_bt_report.sh covering show_instructions (both the known-MAC and <MAC>-placeholder branches) and dump_diagnostics (populated output, the (none loaded)/(rfkill not available) fallbacks, the empty-TARGET_MAC skip, and the (device not known) arm).

verification.evidence: test_bt_report.sh: 24 passed, 0 failed. All fixes lib test files passed -- the eight pre-existing pacman_hook_stall suites stay green alongside the new file.

bt_report.sh: 37/37 lines = 100.00%. Measured through run_all.sh, the subject is_covered() builds. No 'outside kcov's line set' lines were reported, so the figure covers every statement kcov instrumented.
bt_report.sh: 37/37 lines = 100.00%, exit code 0. Second matching run at the --min 100 bar, so a shortfall would have been a non-zero exit rather than a number to misread.
'check_shell_coverage.sh: every checked shell library meets the coverage bar', exit 0, run with the allowlist line already removed so the lib had no exemption.
444 files, 27 clones, 933 duplicated lines = 1.6%, under the 2% threshold. The hook already excludes **/lib/tests/** and **/tests/**, so the shared-core harness design carries no duplication risk.

risks: bt_harness.sh copies _btctl and apply_fix from fix_bluetooth.sh, so a change to either in the entry script would leave the harness stale. This is the same trade-off pacman_hook_stall_harness.sh already makes with log_size, and is preferable to moving those helpers into a lib, which would reintroduce a cross-file-global seam.

The three coverage runs were executed in a detached git worktree under the scratchpad, because a second Claude session was concurrently writing to this repo (phone_focus_mode/config.sh, focus_owner/) and the jail aborts on any working-tree delta during a run. The measurement subject and libs were identical to HEAD; only the tree's isolation differed.
rollback: git revert the commit; that restores the bt_report.sh line in meta/shell-coverage-allowlist.txt and deletes the three new test files together.

After rollback, run bash linux_configuration/scripts/single_use/fixes/lib/tests/run_all.sh and confirm the eight pacman_hook_stall suites still pass, then bash meta/scripts/check_shell_coverage.sh to confirm the gate is green with bt_report.sh exempt again.
